What AI bros and AI companies don't understand is that for anyone to completely trust AI: 1) The AI can't make mistakes; 2) The AI needs to be accountable, aka be legally responsible for everything. I'm an Electronics and Communications Engineer working as a Machine Learning Engineer for the past 6 years, and I haven't studied medicine, mechanical engineering, Accounting, Law, or other fields. For me, trusting what the AI (LLM) is throwing at me in a field I don't know anything about is close to zero atm, without me first reading and learning enough to follow the rabbit hole until I have something to comprehend and challenge the AI's answer in case is wrong or take it as good information to consume/utilize. Now imagine putting your livelihood in the hands of something that has no accountability or incentive to make your life better in any sense of the word. Will you put your well-being, money, safety, etc, in the hands of something like that? I personally won't. Now, I'm not a doomer, etc. I use LLMs every day. It's really good, but right now, they are a tool at our disposal, not a replacement. When we truly get AGI (without true AGI, we can't get ASI, so we might as well call ASI science fiction at this point), then we can have the discussion again.
